Name: Gradual Seasons
Author: opoiuuuu
Description:
[center][size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]Seasons no longer flip overnight.[/b][/color][/size]
In the last week of every season, the next one creeps in bit by bit, and the old one lingers for a few days after the change.[/center]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/55595/55595-1794735153-37694101.png[/img]
[size=2][i]Fall 28, with and without Gradual Seasons[/i][/size][/center]

In Stardew Valley the whole world switches season at once: you go to bed in fall and wake up to a completely white map. [b]Gradual Seasons[/b] blends the seasons into each other instead.

Through the last week of fall, patches of snow settle across the ground, trees drop their leaves and gather snow, snow builds up on your roofs, and rainy days start turning into snow days. By fall 28 most of the valley already looks like winter, so day 1 is a small step instead of a jump. The same happens at every season change: fall colours spread through late summer, and in late winter the snow melts away in patches as spring grass and blossoms break through.

It uses the game's own seasonal art, so everything still looks like Stardew Valley. It follows the in-game date, nothing extra is saved, and you can add or remove it at any time.

[line]

[size=5][color=#8fd3f4][b]New in the latest update (1.1.1)[/b][/color][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Works with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/7332]Way Back Pelican Town[/url][/b] and other retextures that redraw the town for the current season only: their buildings, fences and trees keep their look until the season changes, even with a recolour installed, while the ground around them still changes gradually. No more half-vanilla buildings.[/*]
[*][b]Open source:[/b] the code is now on [url=https://github.com/opoiuuuuu/GradualSeasons]GitHub[/url].[/*]
[/list][b]Added in 1.1.0:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Works with expansion and map mods[/b] like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/3753]Stardew Valley Expanded[/url], Ridgeside Village, Sunberry Village and East Scarp: their maps change gradually too.[/*]
[*][b]Works with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/50334]Seasons of Stardew[/url][/b]: the next season only creeps in at the end of the third month. It's detected automatically.[/*]
[*][b]Smoother changes:[/b] stone paths, snow drifts and snowy roofs from other mods melt in soft patches, with no square edges.[/*]
[/list]The full list of changes is in the [b]Logs[/b] tab.

[line]

[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]What changes[/b][/color][/size]

[size=4][b]The map[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]The game's own next-season tiles appear in natural patches, with soft edges that don't follow the tile grid: snowy ground, frosted cliffs and pond banks, snowy town roofs and big map trees.[/*]
[*]Late fall: snow settles a little more each day. Late winter: the thaw, with spring grass and blossoms breaking through. Late summer: fall's orange ground creeps in. Late spring: summer's ground spreads.[/*]
[*]Ponds, rivers and the sea slowly change colour together, under the game's moving water.[/*]
[*]Stone paths and town squares change colour evenly and stay clear of snow a little longer, while the snow on them melts in the same soft patches as the ground around them.[/*]
[*]Snow drifts piled against trees, fences and cliffs come and go in soft patches too.[/*]
[*]Only ground that really looks different in the next season changes, and the same spots keep their new look as the patches grow, so nothing flickers from day to day.[/*]
[/list]
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/55595/55595-1794735151-1183160699.png[/img]
[size=2][i]The thaw: winter 12, 25 and 28, then spring 2[/i][/size][/center]

[size=4][b]Trees[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Wild trees (oak, maple, pine and mahogany) change in leaf-sized clumps: leaves turn orange and red through late summer, drop and gather snow through late fall, and bud through late winter.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Snow on your roofs[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]The game gives farm buildings no winter look. With this mod, snow builds up on the roofs of the farmhouse, cabins, barns, coops, sheds and stable through late fall, stays all winter and melts in early spring.[/*]
[*]The silo, well, mill, slime hutch and shipping bin get a cap of snow along their top.[/*]
[*]Painted buildings work too: the snow stays white on top of your paint.[/*]
[/list]
[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/55595/55595-1794735147-1873964017.png[/img]
[size=2][i]Snow building up on your farm through late fall[/i][/size][/center]

[size=4][b]Weather particles and ground details[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Snow flurries on dry days in late fall, getting heavier each day, and sleet over the rain.[/*]
[*]Falling autumn leaves in late summer and early winter, and cherry petals in early summer.[/*]
[*]Fallen leaves, petals and summer wildflowers on the ground.[/*]
[*]Particles never double up what the game is already showing, fade in and out smoothly, and are dimmer at night.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]The weather follows along[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Late fall: rain and storms may turn to snow, and clear days sometimes bring early snow. Late winter: snow may turn to rain as the thaw starts. Early spring: the odd late cold snap. Late spring and late summer: storms build and calm.[/*]
[*]The chance grows each day, so full snow days are most likely right before winter.[/*]
[*]Only the main player's game changes the forecast, the same way a Rain Totem does, so the TV forecast and multiplayer stay in sync.[/*]
[*]The forecast is never changed for day 1 of a season, festivals, weddings, Green Rain or weather added by other mods.[/*]
[/list]
[size=4][b]Settings and commands[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Turn every part on or off, choose how many days a season creeps in (0 to 14, normally 7) and lingers (0 to 7, normally 3), and how strong the changes are.[/*]
[*]Console commands: [b]gs_status[/b] shows what the mod is doing today, and [b]gs_preview[/b] followed by a season and day previews that date's map and particles (for example [i]gs_preview fall 28[/i]).[/*]
[*]The map changes also show up in the game's own map screenshots.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]Compatibility[/b][/color][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Expansion and map mods[/b] (Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside Village, Sunberry Village, East Scarp, custom farms and map edits): their areas change along with the rest of the valley, using the same seasonal tile sheets the game switches to on day 1. Areas a mod locks to one season keep their look.[/*]
[*][b]Seasons of Stardew[/b]: the next season creeps in at the end of the third month, and the old one lingers at the start of the first. With it installed, snow days are only added in winter, since that mod clears snow at other times.[/*]
[*][b]Recolours and tile sheet packs[/b] (like DaisyNiko's, Lumisteria's or Xiddav's) change gradually in their own colours.[/*]
[*][b]Art a mod only shows in the current season[/b] (like a seasonal special order board, or the buildings [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/7332]Way Back Pelican Town[/url] redraws each season) is kept as it is until the season changes instead of being painted over, even with a recolour installed. A map whose ground uses a recolour like that simply changes on day 1.[/*]
[*][b]Seasonal building mods[/b] (like Elle's Seasonal Vanilla Buildings): their snowy roofs and frozen fountain melt and settle gradually, and buildings that already look snowy get no extra roof snow.[/*]
[*][b]Other weather mods[/b]: turn off "Change the weather" and keep everything else.[/*]
[/list]
[line]

[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]FAQ[/b][/color][/size]

[b]Does it change when crops grow or die?[/b]
No. Gradual Seasons never changes the date or the season, only how things look (and the weather a little, if you leave that on). Crops grow, ripen and die on the same days as always.

[b]Do snow days water my crops?[/b]
No, just like winter in vanilla. In late fall and early spring a rainy day can turn into a snow day, so check the TV forecast and water your crops on those days, or turn off "Change the weather".

[b]Does it work with my map mod or custom farm?[/b]
It should, as long as its tile sheets come in seasonal versions (spring_, summer_, fall_, winter_), which is how the game itself switches them on day 1 and how most map mods do it. If something looks off, let me know in the comments.

[b]Does it work in multiplayer?[/b]
Yes. Every player who wants to see the changes needs the mod. Only the host's copy changes the weather.

[b]Can I add or remove it mid-save?[/b]
Yes. Nothing is saved to your save file.

[line]

[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]Installation[/b][/color][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install the latest version of [url=https://smapi.io]SMAPI[/url] and start the game through SMAPI once.[/*]
[*]Optional: install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] to change the settings in game.[/*]
[*]Download Gradual Seasons and unzip it into your game's Mods folder. You should end up with [i]Mods/GradualSeasons/manifest.json[/i].[/*]
[*]Start the game through SMAPI. Gradual Seasons should be in the list of loaded mods in the SMAPI console.[/*]
[/list]To change the settings, use Generic Mod Config Menu, or edit [i]Mods/GradualSeasons/config.json[/i] (created the first time you start the game).
To update, replace the GradualSeasons folder (keep your config.json if you changed it). To uninstall, delete the folder; nothing is left behind in your save.

[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]Requirements[/b][/color][/size]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6 or later[/*]
[*]SMAPI 4.0 or later[/*]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu (optional, for changing the settings in game)[/*]
[/list]
[size=5][color=#f2a65a][b]Good to know[/b][/color][/size]
[list]
[*]Ginger Island, the Desert, indoor areas, festivals and any area a mod locks to one season keep their normal look.[/*]
[*]Fruit trees, bushes and things you place (like fences) still change on day 1 of the season.[/*]
[/list]
